speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a very specific direction that was developer-centric and cared about the ecosystem that Pavel and his team were trying to help out with.
zh: 我认为有一个非常具体的方向是以开发者为中​​心并关心生态系统，Pavel 和他的团队试图帮助解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I noticed that they had a very good relationship talking to not just developer evangelists.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

en: In some cases, you can't just build tools to help you out with them because you don't have the underlying instrumentation.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we helped build out the application panel so that you can go in and for any of these features, whether it's debugging service workers or it's debugging your cache or debugging any of these things, you're able to do that.
zh: 所以我们帮助构建了应用程序面板，这样你就可以进入，对于任何这些功能，无论是调试 service workers 还是调试你的缓存或调试其中的任何东西，你都能够做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even though the tool set has expanded over time for each of these eras, I feel like DevTools has been able to keep up, especially as the APIs in the browser has also been evolving over time to meet these moments.
zh: 所以尽管工具集随着时间的推移为这些时代中的每一个都在扩展，我觉得 DevTools 已经能够跟上，特别是随着浏览器中的 API 也在随着时间的推移不断演变以满足这些时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's interesting because I usually, when I look through different companies and their strengths, Microsoft is amazing at building IDEs and so is, for example, JetBrains.
zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为我通常，当我查看不同的公司及其优势时，微软非常擅长构建 IDE，例如，JetBrains 也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for Google, I never felt that Google was any good at building IDEs except for inside of Chrome.
zh: 但对于 Google，我从未觉得 Google 擅长构建 IDE，除了在 Chrome 内部。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever I have to debug a web application, the past many, many years, I use Chrome DevTools because it had...
zh: 每当我必须调试一个 Web 应用程序时，过去的很多年里，我使用 Chrome DevTools，因为它有……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the kind of debug functionality I'm used to having Visual Studio have, which is breakpoints, conditional breakpoints, all sorts of so many debug options from just a performance memory, being able to simulate some of those things.
zh: 我的意思是，我习惯于在 Visual Studio 中拥有的那种调试功能，也就是断点、条件断点，所有各种各样的调试选项，仅从性能内存方面，就能够模拟其中的一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very interesting for me to see that it's almost as if, I'm not sure if this was you, your team, or Google as a whole, but they realized the browser is very important.
zh: 所以对我来说，看到这一点非常有趣，就好像，我不确定这是你、你的团队，还是整个 Google，但他们意识到浏览器非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they built almost like an IDE inside of it.
zh: 所以他们几乎在里面构建了一个 IDE。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can edit the things in line.
zh: 你可以内联编辑这些事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as engineers or as developers, unless you work in front end, you never really notice this.
zh: 我认为作为工程师或开发者，除非你在前端工作，否则你永远不会真正注意到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you do, it's fascinating how it came together.
zh: 但当你注意到时，它是如何结合在一起的是迷人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's really fascinating.
zh: 是的，这真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that, are we in IDE?
zh: 我认为，我们在 IDE 中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Aren't we in IDE?
zh: 我们不在 IDE 中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that a direction we want to go in?
zh: 这是我们想要去的方向吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was always a hot topic for the team.
zh: 这对团队来说一直是个热门话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that where things kind of landed was, well, we want to meet developers where they're at.
zh: 我认为事情最终落点是，嗯，我们想在开发者所在的地方与他们相遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you're always going to have your favorite, you know,
zh: 因为你总是会有你最喜欢的，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: Editor.
zh: 编辑器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we're talking about your control planes for your agents.
zh: 现在我们在谈论你的智能体的控制平面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're always going to have a different surface that you want to primarily work in.
zh: 你总是会有一个你想要主要在其中工作的不同界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as long as DevTools can meet you where you're at and be useful, I think that that's been something the team has tried to do.
zh: 只要 DevTools 能在你所在的地方与你会面并有用，我认为这就是团队一直试图做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We continued having other eras.
zh: 我们继续经历了其他时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yan Gao became our next tech lead after Pavel and helped us through the era of trying to figure out AI is now in the picture and we want to both be able to help humans reason through this massive amount of data that the browser generates for you as well as make it possible for you to connect your agent up to Chrome and DevTools and be able to have it just automate a lot of these journeys for you.
zh: Yan Gao 在 Pavel 之后成为了我们的下一个技术负责人，并帮助我们度过了试图弄清楚 AI 现在已出现在画面中的时代，我们希望能够既帮助人类推理浏览器为你产生的大量数据，也能够使你将你的智能体连接到 Chrome 和 DevTools，并能够让它只是为你自动化许多这些旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that for the first of those problems, I remember anytime I would work with a big site on their performance problems, you could easily spend half a day just looking at traces before you've even written any fixes at all.
zh: 我认为对于第一个问题，我记得每当我在一个大网站上处理他们的性能问题时，你很容易就会花半天时间查看痕迹，甚至在你写下任何修复之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now that we have LLMs, it's very quick to reason through massive stack traces and actually be able to get down to fixes you can make.
zh: 现在我们有了 LLM，通过巨大的堆栈跟踪进行推理并真正能够找到你可以进行的修复是非常快的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just been really, really wonderful to see happen.
zh: 看到这一幕真的非常、非常美妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Addy just described using LLMs to go from massive stack traces to working fixes, which is the perfect moment to talk about our season sponsor, Sentry.
zh: Addy 刚刚描述了使用 LLM 从巨大的堆栈跟踪转变为可行的修复，这是谈论我们赛季赞助商 Sentry 的完美时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably already know what Sentry is because you're a developer.
zh: 你可能已经知道 Sentry 是什么了，因为你是一个开发者。

speaker: Unknown
en: If not, just ask a dev and they'll tell you.
zh: 如果不知道，只要问一个开发者，他们就会告诉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I use Sentry to monitor the backend of the Pragmatic Entry for any and all errors.
zh: 我使用 Sentry 来监控 Pragmatic Entry 的后端的任何及所有错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, Sentry doesn't only do errors.
zh: 当然，Sentry 不仅做错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also have logs, replays, spans, profiles, metrics, and more because they're all connected by the same trace.
zh: 它们还有日志、回放、跨度、配置文件、指标等等，因为它们都由同一个痕迹连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: One new capability Sentry has built that I'm really liking is the ability to fix errors.
zh: Sentry 构建的一个我非常喜欢的新功能是修复错误的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me show you.
zh: 让我给你展示一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the list of errors on my admin backend.
zh: 这是我的管理后端上的错误列表。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a recent error on auth that I want to check out.
zh: auth 上有一个最近的错误，我想查看一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's have CIR run an autofix for us.
zh: 让我们让 CIR 为我们运行一个自动修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: CIR is Sentry's AI debugging tool.
zh: CIR 是 Sentry 的 AI 调试工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, it generates a root cause analysis.
zh: 首先，它生成一个根本原因分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's finding some problem with HTTP versus HTTPS URLs.
zh: 它发现了 HTTP 与 HTTPS URL 的一些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that we know what's going wrong, CIR can create a plan on how to go about fixing it.
zh: 既然我们知道出了什么问题，CIR 可以创建一个关于如何修复它的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could go and edit this plan, but I'm happy with it, so let's create an actual code fix.
zh: 我可以去编辑这个计划，但我对它很满意，所以让我们创建一个实际的代码修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a code fix that CIR generated.
zh: 这是 CIR 生成的代码修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Assuming it looks good, and in my case it does, let's draft a pull request.
zh: 假设它看起来不错，在我的例子中确实如此，让我们起草一个 pull request。

speaker: Unknown
en: And boom, the pull request is created, ready to merge.
zh: 然后 boom，pull request 被创建了，准备好合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I love about autofix is how Sentry went from showing a list of errors inside my application to offering me a fast way to fix it and close the loop while I stay in charge of this bug fix the whole time.
zh: 我喜欢 autofix 的地方在于，Sentry 如何从在我的应用程序中显示错误列表转变为提供一种快速修复它的方法并关闭循环，而我在整个过程中仍然负责这个错误修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Debugging just got a whole lot faster and a whole lot easier.
zh: 调试变得快了很多，也容易了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Check out Sentry at sentry.io slash pragmatic and start detecting errors, diagnosing your root causes, and fixing issues and regressions today.
zh: 请访问 sentry.io slash pragmatic 开始检测错误，诊断根本原因，并今天就修复问题和回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: Addy mentioned things that change when we work with LLMs.
zh: Addy 提到了当我们与 LLM 工作时发生的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing is for sure.
zh: 有一件事是确定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you work with agents, your job is no longer writing code, it's specifying and testing it.
zh: 如果你与智能体一起工作，你的工作不再是编写代码，而是指定和测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this leads us to our presenting sponsor, Antisysys.
zh: 这将我们带到我们的展示赞助商，Antisysys。

speaker: Unknown
en: Antisysys is the most effective method of verifying agentic code today.
zh: Antisysys 是当今验证智能体代码的最有效方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me explain how it works.
zh: 让我解释一下它是如何工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Antisys runs your whole system in a wholesale simulation.
zh: Antisys 在一个批发模拟中运行你的整个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: By doing so, it finds every bug before your users do.
zh: 这样做，它在你的用户之前发现每一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because the simulation is fully deterministic, Antisys doesn't only find bugs, it gives you a perfect reproduction of every issue.
zh: 因为模拟是完全确定性的，Antisys 不仅发现错误，它给你每个问题的完美复现。

speaker: Unknown
en: To create such a tool, the Antisys team needed to invent new kinds of debugging tools as well.
zh: 为了创建这样一个工具，Antisys 团队还需要发明新的调试工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, here's what's called a bug probability graph.
zh: 例如，这就是所谓的错误概率图。

speaker: Unknown
en: The x-axis is virtual time and the y-axis is probability.
zh: x 轴是虚拟时间，y 轴是概率。

speaker: Unknown
en: As Antisys runs the hostile simulations, it plots timeframes when the bug probability increases, which greatly helps with finding the root cause of bugs.
zh: 当 Antisys 运行敌对模拟时，它绘制错误概率增加的时间范围，这极大地有助于找到错误的根本原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Antisys also has a log visualizer.
zh: Antisys 还有一个日志可视化工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vertical lines going down represent events branching off from the same state.
zh: 向下的垂直线代表从同一状态分支出来的事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the purple dots are where the bug happens.
zh: 紫点是错误发生的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Antisys is as good as it gets being able to ship agent-written code.
zh: Antisys 是能够发布智能体编写的代码的最佳选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what teams at Jane Street, Fly.io, and the etcd community use to ship with full confidence.
zh: 这就是 Jane Street、Fly.io 和 etcd 社区的团队用来满怀信心地发布的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Head to antisys.com.tackpragmatic to learn more.
zh: 访问 antisys.com.tackpragmatic 了解更多信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with this, let's get back to Addy and talk about Core Web Vitals.
zh: 有了这个，让我们回到 Addy 并谈谈 Core Web Vitals。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one area that you really pushed, you and the team pushed the industry together is core web vitals.
zh: 有一个领域你真的推动了，你和团队一起推动了行业的发展，那就是核心网页指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, these are a standardized set of metrics to just figure out the real world experience of web pages.
zh: 你知道，这是一套标准化的指标，只是为了弄清楚网页的真实体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of the, you know, before this, again, you would, as a developer, you would measure like, all right, how quick does it render or how quick does it download?
zh: 而且一些，你知道，在此之前，同样，作为开发者，你会衡量，比如，它渲染得有多快或者它下载得有多快？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very simple stuff.
zh: 这是非常简单的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you introduced things like LCP, Largest Contentful Paint, CLS, Cumulative Layout Shift.
zh: 但是你引入了像 LCP，Largest Contentful Paint，CLS，Cumulative Layout Shift 这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: FIE first input delay and then IMP interaction to next paint.
zh: FIE first input delay 然后是 IMP interaction to next paint。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were there.
zh: 你当时就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did the team come up with these things?
zh: 团队是如何想出这些的？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not a web engineer, it takes a little time to understand them, but it does actually explain how users feel.
zh: 如果你不是 Web 工程师，理解它们需要一点时间，但它确实解释了用户的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel you somehow inside of Google managed to connect the kind of feel to a number.
zh: 我觉得你在 Google 内部以某种方式设法将感觉与数字联系起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that the Chrome team has always had an appreciation for user experience research.
zh: 我认为 Chrome 团队一直重视用户体验研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, every time there was a new moment for the web, we'd re-consult that research to understand, well, what are users' expectations and how can we help meet them?
zh: 而且，每当 Web 有新时刻时，我们会重新参考该研究以了解，用户的期望是什么以及我们如何帮助满足它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that we used to reason about performance was
zh: 我们过去用来推理性能的方式是

speaker: Unknown
en: Very much like, hey, is a page loading?
zh: 非常像，嘿，页面正在加载吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what does that even mean?
zh: 这意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, for many people, is the page ready?
zh: 嗯，对许多人来说，页面准备好了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what does ready mean?
zh: 但准备好的意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that mean that I see it?
zh: 这是否意味着我看到了它？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it mean that I can click around it and anything actually happens?
zh: 这是否意味着我可以点击它并且任何事情真的发生了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think for a very long time, we had this almost nebulous way of thinking about page load times.
zh: 所以我认为很长一段时间以来，我们都有这种几乎模糊的思考页面加载时间的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the team felt like it was finally time to come up with a more nuanced perspective around how we reason about performance.
zh: 团队觉得终于到了围绕我们如何推理性能提出更细致的观点的时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you break it down, there are a number of key moments across the user's journey that they care about.
zh: 所以如果你分解它，在用户旅程中有许多关键时刻，他们关心这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it happening?
zh: 它正在发生吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is anything loading?
zh: 有任何东西正在加载吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see a header?
zh: 你能看到页头吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see a spinner?
zh: 你能看到加载图标吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see anything at all?
zh: 你能看到任何东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something useful there for you?
zh: 那里有什么对你有用的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe that's a header image.
zh: 所以那可能是一个页头图片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's a hero image.
zh: 可能是一个首屏图片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it is a hero video.
zh: 可能是一个首屏视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's like the core piece of content on the page.
zh: 可能就像页面上核心的内容块。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it useful?
zh: 它有用吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it usable?
zh: 它可用吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of these different moments can correlate to these different metrics.
zh: 所有这些不同的时刻都可以与这些不同的指标相关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for things like your hero image, you can think about that as your largest contentful paint.
zh: 所以对于像你的首屏图片这样的东西，你可以把它看作你的最大内容绘制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not going to generalize across every page.
zh: 这不会推广到每个页面。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some cases, the image may not be the most important thing.
zh: 在某些情况下，图片可能不是最重要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might be, you know, the article text.
zh: 可能是，你知道，文章文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: There may be cases where, you know, you want to be able to interact fairly quickly with a page.
zh: 可能存在这样的情况，你知道，你希望能够相当快地与页面进行交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can remember many times over the years when I might be shopping and whether it's on my phone or on my desktop, I will click like the add to cart button and just crickets.
zh: 这些年来我能记得很多次，当我在购物时，无论是在手机上还是在桌面上，我会点击那个加入购物车按钮，然后就是一片死寂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing will happen.
zh: 什么都不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because JavaScript did not load or maybe the event handler was not attached because not all elements finished loading.
zh: 因为 JavaScript 没有加载，或者可能事件处理器没有附加，因为并非所有元素都完成了加载。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know as engineers what's happening, but as a user, it's like... Yeah, as a user, like, wait, what's happening?
zh: 我们作为工程师知道发生了什么，但作为用户，就像……是的，作为用户，就像，等等，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this stuff can happen where you just tap, tap, tap, the event handler gets attached and now you're adding it like twice or three times, but you don't know.
zh: 这种情况可能会发生，你只是点击，点击，点击，事件处理器被附加了，现在你把它加了两次或三次，但你不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans are shockingly simple.
zh: 人类惊人地简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the experience you have with somebody that's just trying to cross the street, if the light doesn't turn, doesn't say they can walk fast enough, they'll just keep hitting that button.
zh: 如果你想想你与一个只是想过马路的人的体验，如果灯不亮，不说他们可以足够快地走，他们就会一直按那个按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the same experience they have on the internet.
zh: 这就是他们在互联网上的相同体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there were other aspects of user experience that I think we acknowledge were actually kind of problematic.
zh: 我认为用户体验还有其他方面，我认为我们承认实际上确实是有问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One big one was over the years, obviously, sites tried to monetize as heavily as they could.
zh: 一个很大的方面是这些年来，显然，网站试图尽可能多地变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you would see not just banner ads, but you'd see modals, you'd see all of these things thrown up in front of your face.
zh: 所以你不仅会看到横幅广告，还会看到模态框，你会看到所有这些东西扔在你面前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if you set aside, maybe there's some validity around a business needs to monetize.
zh: 即使你撇开这一点，也许商业需要变现有一些合理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things shouldn't cause a really bad experience.
zh: 这些东西不应该导致非常糟糕的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm on a page that has a bunch of ads, I shouldn't start reading an article and then suddenly everything gets pushed down, right?
zh: 如果我在一个有一堆广告的页面上，我不应该开始读一篇文章然后突然所有东西都被推下去了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because the ad is finally loaded.
zh: 只是因为广告终于加载了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's where cumulative layout shift kind of comes from.
zh: 这就是累积布局偏移产生的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this idea that, hey, we should be trying to keep that page stable so the user has a good time.
zh: 这个想法是，嘿，我们应该努力保持页面稳定，这样用户才能玩得开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of iteration around how do we define these metrics in a way that captures a few of these different use cases that are very nuanced because the internet is not all that homogenous.
zh: 关于我们如何定义这些指标，以捕捉一些非常微妙的这些不同用例，有很多迭代，因为互联网并不是完全同质的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where we begin to see more of these roles converge.

speaker: Unknown
en: So the engineer that also has product sense, the product person that also has engineering sense or UX sense, the UX person that also cares about product,

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你希望在智能体变得更好的同时，放大你自己的理解。

speaker: Unknown
